story_title: Designing AI Agents to Resist Prompt Injection
why_this_story: As AI agents gain autonomous capabilities to take real-world actions, prompt injection changes from a minor text quirk into a critical security threat. OpenAI's public framework detailing how they defend ChatGPT agents provides an essential blueprint for the entire industry.
viral_angle: AI agents can be hijacked by invisible text inside emails or websites—here is how OpenAI is attempting to fix the unfixable flaw.
story_sentence: Everyone thinks AI prompts just need better guardrails, but OpenAI reveals that securing autonomous agents requires architectural isolation of actions and sensitive data.

caption:
AI agents are gaining the power to perform real-world actions—from reading emails to managing cloud databases. But that autonomy introduces a critical vulnerability: prompt injection.

OpenAI released technical guidance detailing how they design ChatGPT agents to resist social engineering and malicious context injections.

The key takeaway? System prompts alone cannot guarantee security. Securing an agent requires architectural isolation: treating untrusted data separately and enforcing strict API privilege boundaries.

Here is how the threat works and how the defense architecture is changing.
